note: Every byte below is derived from fixed labels; regenerate with the generator, never by hand. Hex is lower-case throughout.

constants.challenge_layout: nonce(16) || HMAC-SHA256(relay_secret, challenge_domain || identity_hash(16) || u64be(registration_seq) || nonce(16))

A.description: the relay every vector is presented to

B.description: another relay; its challenges must be refused at A

lowx.note: X25519 half is the all-zero (low-order) point: the Ed25519 signature verifies, but no session token can be encrypted to it.

registrations.description: Retichat-js browser, first signed registration at relay A: no signed row exists for the identity, so the challenge's MAC binds seq 0 and the relay INSERTs.

The same browser re-registering after a 401 (session lost): its row is at seq 1, so the challenge's MAC binds seq 1 and the relay UPDATEs the row in place to seq 2. The name carries non-ASCII characters to pin UTF-8.

Reticulum-rust gateway (or Python PostInterface) in wake mode, signing with its persistent transport identity (no relay lists it: peering is open): client reticulum-php, mode 6, with peer_url / peer_interface_id / peer_session_token covered by the signature. Its row is at seq 5.
The same gateway identity in poll mode (no wake_url): client rns-post-interface with the transport field, no peer fields (signed as empty strings). First registration, seq 0.

PHP relay B registering at relay A exactly as a gateway does (section 10): signed with B's persistent relay identity (the identity file), client reticulum-php, mode 1, peer_url = B's canonical host_url, the peer fields random per registration. First registration, seq 0.

negative.description: browser-first with the name changed after signing.
browser-first with bitrate changed after signing.
gateway-wake with peer_url changed after signing.
gateway-wake with peer_session_token changed after signing.
browser-first's exact signed bytes, signed by a different identity, presented with the browser's public key.
browser-first replayed verbatim after it succeeded. The signature is valid, but the row is now at seq 1 and the challenge's MAC bound seq 0.
A correctly signed gateway registration over a challenge relay A issued while the row was at seq 4, presented after the row moved to seq 5.
A correctly signed browser registration, addressed to relay A, over a challenge minted by relay B (different relay_secret). Same identity, same seq: only the MAC differs.
The browser signs (validly) a challenge relay A issued for another identity. The MAC covers the identity hash, so it fails for the browser's hash.
The browser flips one bit of the nonce inside a real seq-0 challenge and signs the result validly. The MAC no longer matches: a client cannot alter a challenge.
browser-first plus metadata.identity_hash naming another identity (not a signed field, so the signature still verifies).
browser-first plus metadata.wake_url, a key the signature does not cover.
browser-first with the public key in upper-case hex. Hex fields are lower-case only.
A correctly signed rns-js registration with mode 6 (gateway). Browsers are endpoints: modes 3, 5 and 6 are refused for client rns-js.
A correctly signed rns-js registration that names a peer_url. A browser row may not carry peer fields: they would make it look like a PHP peer and draw wakes to any URL.
A correctly signed registration with client "x". Only rns-js, reticulum-php and rns-post-interface may register signed.
The gateway, correctly signed, client reticulum-php with no peer fields. A wake-mode gateway must name where it is woken.
The gateway, correctly signed, client rns-post-interface carrying a peer_url. A poll-mode gateway is never woken, so it may not name a URL.
A correctly signed first registration (a new row) while relay A's interfaces table is at max_interface_rows and nothing is reclaimable.

A correctly signed browser registration whose public key has the all-zero (low-order) X25519 half. The Ed25519 signature verifies, but no token can be encrypted to the key, so the relay refuses it before writing anything.

tokens_negative.description: browser-first's encrypted token with one ciphertext bit flipped: the HMAC fails, decryption must fail, the client must not use it.
browser-first's encrypted token decrypted by the gateway identity: a token is readable only by the identity it was encrypted to.

url_canonical.note: host lower-cased, trailing slash dropped; the path keeps its case
scheme lower-cased, default port and /v1/wake dropped
path case is significant: a different key
an IDN look-alike in ASCII form: valid, and a different key
a non-ASCII look-alike: refused, never folded onto retichat.com

positive.description: Relay A confirms the wake URL stored for the gateway-wake row (canonical peer_url) before it ever wakes it. The gateway's config writes its node_url with a trailing slash: it compares canonical forms.

gateway_refusals.description: A confirm for another identity's row. The gateway signs only for its own transport identity.
A confirm from a relay this gateway does not register with (its node_url is relay A). The gateway is not a signing oracle for anyone else.
A confirm naming a wake URL that is not this gateway's own.
The nonce in upper-case hex. Hex fields are lower-case only.
A confirm body with a key outside the five.

answer_negative.description: The right bytes, signed by another identity.
The gateway's signature over another nonce (an earlier confirm's answer).
The gateway's signature for another wake URL.
The gateway's signature for relay B's confirm.
The gateway's registration signature (vector gateway-wake) offered as the answer. The domains keep the two apart.
The nonce echoed back. Reaching the URL is not enough: the answer must be signed by the row's key.
The right signature in upper-case hex.
The right signature with a second key.
A server without the handler (an older gateway binary) answers 404.

php_relay_peer.identity_file_layout: x25519_private(32) || ed25519_seed(32): the 64 bytes RNS Identity.to_file writes

decrypt_negative.description: The good blob with its ephemeral public key replaced by 32 zero bytes: the X25519 result is all zero, so it is refused before any key is derived.
The good blob with one bit of its HMAC flipped.
The gateway-wake vector's token, encrypted to the gateway: the HMAC fails under relay B's keys.
A correctly encrypted blob whose plaintext is not 64 lower-case hex: it decrypts, and is refused as a protocol error.

confirm.description: Relay A confirms relay B's wake URL (its canonical host_url) after B's registration, before it ever wakes B. B's [interfaces] writes relay A's node_url with a trailing slash: it compares canonical forms.

confirm_refusals.description: A confirm for the gateway's identity, sent to relay B.
A confirm from a relay that is not in relay B's [interfaces].
A confirm naming relay A's URL as relay B's wake URL.

confirm_answer_negative.description: The right bytes signed by the gateway's key, not relay B's.

transport_id.rule: REGISTRATION.md section 10.2 (revision 7): the transport id is the identity hash, SHA-256(x25519_pub || ed25519_pub)[:16] of the identity file, and is the only id the relay writes; the pre-switch id (transport_state.identity_hash_hex) stays its own too

sent.description: A link request for the browser's lxmf.delivery destination, as its sender packs it (HEADER_1, hops 0), before it is put into transport.

transport_id.into_transport: flags = HEADER_2 << 6 | TRANSPORT << 4 | (flags & 0x0f); raw = flags || hops || next_hop(16) || raw[2:] (RNS 1.5.2 Transport.outbound, Transport.py:1397-1403)

packets.description: The sender learned its path from an announce relay B relayed after the switch: the next hop is B's transport id. B forwards it.
The sender learned its path before the switch: the next hop is B's pre-switch id. B still forwards it.
The next hop is another transport node (the gateway's identity hash): not B's. B's packet filter refuses it.
